datum.H_Abar: XXZ chain on qubits 1..7: J (X X + Y Y) + Jz Z Z nearest-neighbour, J=1.0, Jz=0.5, longitudinal fields h = [0.3,-0.7,0.5,-0.2,0.8,-0.4,0.6] (fixed disorder; no known integrability; H_Abar conserves total Z of the bath, and the full H conserves the Z-parity of all 8 qubits; nothing below needs non-integrability)
datum.preparation_S1: rho_A(0) = |+><+| ; rho_Abar(0) = exp(-beta H_Abar)/Z, beta = 1.0 (mixed global state)
datum.instruments: projective Z and X measurements on A; Born rule p = Tr(rho_A E)
datum.external_time: parameter t of the global unitary; grid t in [0, 40] step 0.1
datum.units: hbar = 1, energies in units of omega0

BLP.grid_note: sum over the 0.1 grid: a lower bound on the continuous Breuer-Laine-Piilo measure
BLP.note: Any positive increment of the trace distance between two reduced states is information backflow (Breuer-Laine-Piilo); a Markovian (CP-divisible) reduced dynamics would make D non-increasing.

cptp_check.note: For a product preparation with a fixed bath state, rho_A(0) -> rho_A(t) is a linear CPTP map (standard).

tcl.note: K(t) = dPhi_t/dt Phi_t^{-1} is the exact time-convolutionless generator of the derived reduced dynamics; it is time dependent (no fixed Lindbladian) and depends on the bath preparation (kernel is downstream of the state).

cp_divisibility.note: A negative Choi eigenvalue of an intermediate map means the derived reduced dynamics is not CP-divisible (non-Markovian).

S4_initial_correlations.note_converse: The Zparity case has Q rho(0) = eps Z^(x8) != 0 but [H, Z^(x8)] = 0, so the inhomogeneous term vanishes identically and the futures coincide: the inhomogeneous term vanishes IF the preparation is rho_A (x) rho_ref, not only if.
S4_initial_correlations.note: Two global preparations with identical rho_A(0) AND identical rho_Abar(0) evolve to different rho_A(t). No map on rho_A(0) alone (nor on both marginals) reproduces both futures; the Nakajima-Zwanzig inhomogeneous term carries the difference (its t = 0 value is recorded; for the classical Z0Z1 correlation the first two orders vanish at t = 0 and the difference appears at third order in t). Standard initial-correlation result (Pechukas 1994; Stelmachovic-Buzek 2001).

models.a_nonintegrable_XXZ_disordered: XXZ chain on qubits 1..7: J (X X + Y Y) + Jz Z Z nearest-neighbour, J=1.0, Jz=0.5, longitudinal fields h = [0.3,-0.7,0.5,-0.2,0.8,-0.4,0.6] (fixed disorder; no known integrability; H_Abar conserves total Z of the bath, and the full H conserves the Z-parity of all 8 qubits; nothing below needs non-integrability)
models.b_single_spin: H_Abar = omega0/2 Z_1 (one bath qubit), thermal at beta=1
models.c_clean_XX_chain: J (XX+YY) chain on 7 qubits, Jz=0, no fields (free fermions), thermal at beta=1

model_b_prime_exact_recurrence.note: A closed complement with commensurate spectrum returns A exactly to its prepared state: relaxation is not forced.

S5_nonunique_local_law.note: Closure fixes nothing about the local law of A: the same subsystem datum with different (closed) complements has different reduced dynamics.

S6_records_and_interventions.construction: Omega' = A u Abar u R (9 qubits); H' = H x I_R; record written at t1=3 by the unitary CNOT(A->R), applied as an externally timed intervention (a supplied control and clock, not generated by H'); readout at t2=6.
S6_records_and_interventions.note_two_time: The uninterrupted one-time map gives 0.449; composing one-time maps with the instrument (bath re-prepared at t1) gives the composed value; the exact closed-whole result with the record written differs from both. Multi-time statistics are properties of the process (process tensor), not of Phi_t. Two recorded equalities are identities, not evidence: register population = Born probability (CNOT with a fresh |0> is a Stinespring dilation of Z-dephasing on A), and unitary record = measure-and-forget (the idle register commutes with the partial trace).
S6_records_and_interventions.note_persistence: With [H', Z_R] = 0 the register is unchanged. kappa X_R alone rotates the record out of the fixed Z_R readout basis but loses no information (optimal readout success stays 1). kappa X_R X_7 couples the register to the bath and the recorded bit becomes genuinely less retrievable from R. Record persistence is a property of the supplied dynamics, not of closure.

S7_time_reversal.note: The conjugated final state is an admissible preparation of the same closed whole; rho_rev(t) = rho(T-t)^* exactly, so its forward evolution is the original run read backwards: S_A returns non-monotonically to 0 at t = 40. Closure supplies no arrow; the low-entropy preparation does.

mixed_S1_trajectory.note: Both inequalities are saturated at t = 0 (product state with pure A) and strict afterwards; on a pure global state they reduce to S_A = S_Abar and test nothing more.

S8_what_closure_forces.note: Closure forces: unitarity (global purity and entropy constant), conservation of the fixed global H, S_A = S_Abar for a pure global state, subadditivity and Araki-Lieb (checked on the mixed trajectory), and eventual quasi-recurrence in finite dimension. All are theorems of standard quantum mechanics; none is a GRUT contribution.

S9_equivariant_state_selection_is_statio.note: A unitarily equivariant selection rule F(H) yields a stationary state: every restriction is frozen. A selection rule with local dynamical content must depend on more than H (the access structure, a clock, or a non-equivariant datum).

cases.preparation: |+> (x) excited bath eigenstate (the S8 pure preparation)

S10_equilibration_on_average.note: Closure plus the generic hypothesis of non-degenerate energy gaps forces equilibration ON AVERAGE: the infinite-time average of D(rho_A(t), omega_A) is bounded by (1/2) sqrt(d_A^2/d_eff). The size of the bound is set by the supplied preparation through d_eff; it does not force pointwise or monotone relaxation, a thermal omega_A, or a time scale.

athermality_budget.sigma: Gibbs state of the global H at beta = 1 (any stationary sigma works)
athermality_budget.note: Closure alone: D(rho_Omega(t)||sigma) is conserved for stationary sigma, and monotonicity of relative entropy under partial trace gives D(rho_A(t)||Tr_Abar sigma) <= D(rho_Omega(0)||sigma) at every t, for every subsystem.

second_law_identity.hypothesis: rho_Omega(0) = rho_A(0) (x) gamma_Abar with gamma_Abar the Gibbs state of H_Abar at beta = 1 (the S1 preparation)
second_law_identity.definition: Sigma(t) = [S_A(t) - S_A(0)] + beta [E_Abar(t) - E_Abar(0)],  E_Abar = Tr(H_Abar rho)
second_law_identity.note: Esposito-Lindenberg-Van den Broeck identity Sigma = I(A:Abar) + D(rho_Abar||gamma_Abar) >= 0 at every t (exact, from global unitarity). Pointwise non-negative but not monotone; Landauer's erasure bound follows from it.
